title: Lung anatomy: lobes, bronchi and alveoli
description: Explore lung lobes, airways and alveoli, then compare Type I and II pneumocytes in a separate microscopic-scale teaching illustration.

questions.question: What are the lobes of the right and left lungs?
questions.answer: The right lung usually has superior, middle and inferior lobes; the left has superior and inferior lobes with a cardiac notch. Fissures divide the lobes, though normal anatomy can vary.

questions.question: Where does air go after the bronchi?
questions.answer: Air passes from progressively smaller bronchi to bronchioles, then through the respiratory zone toward alveoli. Exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide occurs across the very thin alveolar–capillary barrier.

questions.question: What is a Type I pneumocyte?
questions.answer: A Type I pneumocyte is a very thin squamous cell forming much of the alveolar gas-exchange surface. It can be recognized on the separate microscopic-scale teaching illustration, not on the whole-lung image.

questions.question: What does a Type II pneumocyte do?
questions.answer: A Type II pneumocyte is a plumper alveolar cell that secretes pulmonary surfactant, which helps reduce surface tension. It also contributes to maintenance and repair of the alveolar lining.

questions.question: Is the enlarged alveolar image an actual microscope slide?
questions.answer: No. It is a digital educational illustration that shows the thin Type I lining next to a plumper Type II cell. It is not histology or a literal magnification of the macroscopic lung image.
